content.text: I have reviewed the entire agreement. There is no audit, inspection, verification, or records-examination right running against AP anywhere in the document.

input.quote: Customer agrees to provide all reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services in a timely and effective manner.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right exercisable by Kubient against AP. The fee mechanic (§5) is revenue-share reported and collected by Kubient (with Impressions "as measured by Kubient"), so there is nothing for Kubient to audit at AP, and neither §1, §5 nor §6 (Use of Service) gives Kubient any right to inspect AP's records, premises or systems. The only access obligation on AP — "reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services" (§1) — is service-delivery cooperation, not an audit or verification right, and confers no right to enter AP premises or connect to AP systems. Because no audit right binds AP at all, AP's position is better than the preferred limits (frequency, notice, independent auditor, cost allocation, no system access), and there is nothing to redline; adding audit machinery would only create a Vendor right that does not exist today. Note for the file: if Kubient later requests reconciliation or audit language, we would insist on the preferred parameters (once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, off-site where possible, Kubient's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct access to AP systems).
